newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, Eurodollars sluggish ahead Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, Eurodollars sluggish ahead Greenspan.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Eurodollar futures made slow progress on Tuesday as interest was thin after a U.S. holiday and ahead of Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to the U.S. Senate banking committee.
Dealers said a lack of news and the Tokyo stock market's relative composure after Monday's steep decline hampered interest in Euroyen futures.
"Locals were selling Euroyen near the highs but it was in a very tight range all day," said a trader with a Japanese house.
"The news coming out of Tokyo is still not that good. The Nikkei's not strong so that should give support to the Euroyen market."
The 225-share Nikkei average lost 122.18 points to end at 17,358.16 after hitting a low of 17,282.69.

September Euroyen was quoted at 99.30 at 1115 GMT against its previous SIMEX close at 99.32. Turnover was a light 2,160 lots. The contract was not traded in Chicago overnight due to the Martin Luther King Jr. holiday.
Japanese government bond (JGB) futures settled at 126.04 against their opening 126.28.
Eurodollar futures finished scarcely changed with the June contract at 94.17 against its previous close at 94.20.
"Locals are more willing to short the market because the chances of a rate hike are still in the market," said the trader, adding, however, that a 25 basis point hike was being discounted by players.
